answer: Stop sybils with a voyage forge quill: an agent bonds one voyage route. Each cycle it forges one quill nib at its forge and signs the log; verifiers match the nib's ink strokes to the route chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 voyages at 19x: one quill inks once on one voyage, its strokes set by that forge alone, unrepeatable elsewhere, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents sign once, keep rights.
